reviewer: OMP agent (M12 workspace, cache, and reclaim)
note: SPACE-010 deliver watcher events: an editor's operations are not all writes - a save may be an ordinary write, an atomic replacement (write a temporary file and rename it over the target), a rename, or a delete - and src/space/watcher.zig speaks inotify directly so the events are the kernel's and the masks are the kernel's, with the mask-to-kind mapping documented beside it. The module is Linux-only and says so at compile time: elsewhere the type resolves to a stub whose methods return Unsupported, so a machine without the mechanism cannot be mistaken for a workspace without changes. It found two real bugs by being run: the first was an unaligned view of the event buffer, which panicked rather than misbehaving quietly and is now an aligned copy; the second was worse and was caught by the test - one read returns several events and the first version returned only the first, so the second half of a rename was dropped, which is exactly the half a sync needs to know where a file went. The test drives the four operations on a native Linux workspace and looks for the documented change in each batch rather than dictating the count, because the kernel legitimately reports a save as a creation and a close-write. Evidence is recorded inside the WSL2 guest, so actualPlatform is genuinely linux-x86_64. Fault proof: returning only the first event of a read makes the rename assertions fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
